prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Evidence is still thin for specific change types because no change type has at least two tests agreeing after noise correction.
Redesigning friend selection (adoption, redesign) and moving sign-in (sign_in, reorder) were helpful, winning their tests.
Updating onboarding intro story copy (choose_path, copy) made performance worse.
No clear effect was seen for waiting step info (home, wait_info), notification toggles (home, notification), or layout changes (finish, layout).
Predictions were consistently too high compared to noise-corrected measured outcomes.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, redesign: +6.8% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- choose_path, copy: -3.3% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- finish, layout: -1.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, notification: +2.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- home, wait_info: +1.7% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)
- sign_in, reorder: +3.5% after noise correction, 1 test(s) (one test only: weak evidence, not a pattern yet)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 76.0%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 69.8%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 21.3%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [finish, new_screen] Pet interaction visual tips screen: Add a dedicated visual guide screen before finishing onboarding to demonstrate how to click, drag, and interact with the pet. (why: Support mailbox received 3 complaints about confusion over controlling or hiding the pet, and finish step conversion is 64.8%.)
1: [sign_in, reorder] Move sign-in after adoption certificate: Move sign-in screen to appear right after adoption certificate confirmation, before the setup waiting screen. (why: Capitalizes on emotional investment after finalizing the pet adoption certificate before asking users to sign in.)
2: [adoption, new_flow] Photo validation check sub-flow: Insert a dedicated photo verification screen to confirm quality and lighting before pet generation. (why: 3 support emails reported custom pet generation failing or rendering incorrectly during adoption.)
3: [adoption, layout] Checklist layout for photo upload screen: Switch the photo upload screen layout to a checklist format highlighting recommended photo guidelines. (why: Adoption conversion is 69.8% with 1017s mean time, and users reported custom pet image errors.)
4: [home, wait_info] Desktop launch info on waiting screen: Add system launch updates and tips to the waiting screen detailing desktop overlay setup progress. (why: Waiting stage mean time is 2336s, and 3 support tickets reported pets failing to appear on the desktop view.)
5: [choose_path, copy] Clear path option copy revision: Update headline and body on the choose_path screen to succinctly differentiate preset selection from custom pet creation. (why: choose_path has a high mean duration of 514s and 23.8% dropoff, indicating user confusion when choosing.)
6: [finish, hint] Desktop shortcut hint on home intro: Display a helpful hint on the home_intro screen explaining key shortcuts to bring hidden pets to the foreground. (why: Finish step dropoff is 35.2% and support received reports of pets missing on screen or app failing to open.)
